cells.tense: You are holding something you chose and it is still answering back to you.
cells.ask: Name one thing you'd keep even if nothing about it ever improved again.
cells.core:
There's a thing you're carrying that you can actually feel. A direction, some work, maybe a way you've decided to live. And you're still the one who decides it. You didn't inherit it and you're not performing it. That's why it holds. You're not steady because you're certain. You're steady because the thing and the feeling about it run in the same direction, and you'd know the difference if they didn't.

Keep it easy. When the day gets loud, you don't have to relitigate the decision. Check the one thing you'd keep even if nothing about it ever improved again, and let that be enough for today. The pull of it may fade in and out; that's normal. Let the rest catch up on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You chose this, and you're still the one choosing it.
cells.verb: feeling what was imagined until it is real
cells.place: the room where you decide what this is for

cells.tense: You are already living past the ending, guarding a thing nobody asked you to defend.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're tending and leave it alone today, unwatered and fine.
cells.core:
You've got one eye on a version of this that isn't here yet. Somewhere ahead the thing arrives complete and it's finally safe. So you keep checking on it. You go over it again at night, you plan the next version, you defend it before anyone has touched it. None of that is keeping it safe. It's keeping you from finishing anything.

Caring for something doesn't mean keeping it in sight at all times. Pick the one thing you're tending and leave it be today. Not forever, just today. Unwatered and fine. Watch the difference between what actually needs you and what you've decided needs you.

cells.tense: You stopped pointing at things a while back and called the stopping sensible.
cells.ask: Go back to one thing you put down and pick it up exactly as it was.
cells.core:
There's a thing you put down. You know which one. Maybe the timing was wrong or you got a reaction you didn't want, or somewhere along the line it stopped seeming reasonable to keep at it. So you set it down, and not wanting it got comfortable. You can make decisions fine. You can tell what this week needs, what other people need. What's hard to find is a shape of your own to point at and say yes to.

Nothing is wrong with the engine. Pick it up as it was, at whatever size it has left. You don't have to know why. Point at it and move one step.

cells.tense: You are steering this, and talking about it like the weather is steering.
cells.ask: Name the one you're already leaning toward, before it's sorted out, as yours.
cells.core:
You've been making choices here and calling them obvious. The thing you do, the thing you keep, the thing you've quietly started moving toward. You say anyone in your spot would do the same, that it isn't a decision, it's just how it is. And you're not lying to anyone. You just haven't been counting it. The steering is happening. Whoever's been doing it isn't getting the credit.

You don't have to make a piece of it. Say out loud which way you're already leaning, before it's sorted. Yes, before you're sure. You're allowed to change direction later. Starting now means the choice is one you can see.
cells.sheetLine: The steering is happening. Your name isn't on it yet.
